Project One • Ottawa • Spring 2027

Restoring Algonquin Presence

From acknowledgement to presence. A three-cart pilot designed to create visible, lower-barrier space for Algonquin food businesses, makers, artists and emerging entrepreneurs in Ottawa.

This is not simply a plan to operate three food carts. It is a plan to build shared commercial infrastructure that can put Algonquin entrepreneurship in places where residents, workers and visitors can actually see it.

Why this exists

Acknowledgement and presence are not the same thing.

Ottawa acknowledges that it sits on the unceded and unsurrendered territory of the Algonquin Anishinaabe Nation. That acknowledgement is heard across the capital every day.

The question behind this project is practical: what would it look like if some of that acknowledgement became visible, everyday Algonquin economic participation?

Restoring Algonquin Presence is being developed as one answer: build the infrastructure first, establish high-visibility opportunities, and create a platform that can grow beyond Chelsea's Kitchen.

The 2027 pilot

Three carts. One platform. More room to begin.

The first pilot is now focused on three professionally built mobile carts. Each cart is intended to be flexible enough to support different kinds of Algonquin enterprise while creating a recognizable public presence across Ottawa.

01

Build the infrastructure

Professionally constructed, equipped mobile vending carts designed for repeated use in high-visibility public and visitor spaces.

02

Prove the model

Chelsea's Kitchen helps establish operations, customer traffic and a workable commercial model during the pilot phase.

03

Open the opportunity

Create pathways for additional Algonquin entrepreneurs to test products, concepts and businesses without first carrying the cost of a storefront.

What can happen here

More than food.

A cart is infrastructure. The value is what Algonquin entrepreneurs can do with it.

The pilot is intended to test how shared, mobile commercial infrastructure can lower barriers to market entry while building a distinctive Algonquin presence within Ottawa's tourism and visitor economy.

The principle

Build the opportunity first.

We build the carts. We build the operating model. We build the partnerships. Then we work with Ottawa to make space for something launch-ready.

How the pilot gets there

From idea to visible presence.

Build partnerships

Bring together Algonquin participants, businesses, sponsors, institutions and organizations that can help move the project forward.

Fund & build 3 carts

Secure the construction, equipment, branding and operating resources needed for the pilot.

Develop the participation model

Create fair scheduling, operating, training and participation systems so the infrastructure can support more than one business.

Launch & measure

Test three carts in visible Ottawa settings, measure demand and participation, learn from the pilot and grow carefully.

TRC Week 2026

Do something useful now while we build something bigger.

For every $5 contributed through this campaign, Chelsea's Kitchen commits to distributing one portion of baked bannock and chili in downtown Ottawa in early October.

That is the immediate commitment. The larger purpose is to keep developing the infrastructure, partnerships and operating model behind the three-cart 2027 pilot.

What contributions support

Campaign funds support the work involved in Restoring Algonquin Presence, including the TRC Week food commitment, supplies and equipment, cart development and construction planning, project design, outreach, partnerships and related operating costs.

Transparency: Contributions are made to Chelsea's Kitchen. They are not charitable donations and do not qualify for charitable tax receipts.

Restoring Algonquin Presence is an evolving small-business-led project. Locations, partners, operating arrangements and timelines remain subject to permissions, funding and agreements.

The destination

Algonquin-led. Entrepreneur-focused. Built for long-term presence.

The carts are the beginning. The goal is a durable platform through which Algonquin people can sell, create, experiment, build businesses and be visibly present in the economic life of the capital.
